description_en: Theguthi(ritual association) responsible for thisdyaḥcheṃ(god-house) consists of seven members from the Jyāpu community. Among them, the senior-most member holds the title ofāḥju, who, according to traditional custom, must reside in thedyaḥcheṃafter death.Within the ancient urban core of Patan, three distinct forms of Gaṇeśa are venerated, each bearing a unique epithet based on location and iconography. The Gaṇeśa enshrined in the eastern quarter is known asThaina Gaṇeśa, the one in the west asKwayna Gaṇeśa, and the deity in the central part of the city asBuina Gaṇeśa. Their names derive from Newar spatial terminology. In Newar,thãmeans “above,” referring to the eastern Gaṇeśa who is depicted seated atop Bhairava and hence calledThaina Gaṇeśa. The termkwaymeans “below,” and the western deity, represented as sitting beneath Bhairava, is accordingly calledKwayna Gaṇeśa. The wordbuinameans “pressed under the arm,” signifying the central Gaṇeśa held under Bhairava’s arm, henceBuina Gaṇeśa. This triadic iconography of Gaṇeśa and Bhairava, which emerged in Patan during the late medieval period, exemplifies a local adaptation of tantric visual conventions (M. Ācārya VS 2079, pp. 100–108). The presentdyaḥcheṃhouses theKwayna Gaṇeśa.Unlike other images of Kwayna Gaṇeśa found elsewhere in Patan that depict the deity beneath Bhairava in sculptural form, thisdyaḥcheṃenshrines only a brassmukhākṛti(mask). Beside the main mask, a smaller one is also installed, both regarded as manifestations of Kwayna Gaṇeśa. The principal brass mask is placed on a brass throne (siṃhāsana), donated by anAmātyaof Patan in (1861 CE) VS 1918. The room housing the mask is ornamented with metal lions, flags, and arches (toraṇas). The present concrete building of thedyaḥcheṃ, surmounted by a dome (fūchāorpur), was constructed only in 1981–82 CE (VS 2038). Previously, this site was occupied by the historicalPaleswã Pukhū(Lotus Pond). The temple’s construction became possible through extensive voluntary labor (śramadāna) contributed by the local residents (currentāḥju, Mahārjan, male, age 85).Prior to the erection of the presentdyaḥcheṃ, a distinct custom concerning the Kwayna Gaṇeśa prevailed in Naḥ Ṭol. Seven senior Jyāpu members from Naḥ Ṭola, Chāḥ Bahāḥ, and Chobhar formed the hereditaryguthiof Kwayna Gaṇeśa. Among them, the eldest was known asāḥju. Before the establishment of thedyaḥcheṃin 1983 CE (VS 2040), the brass mask of Kwayna Gaṇeśa (LAL2970-001) was kept in theāḥju’s private residence. Worship was performed there, followed by a communal feast (bhwoj). Upon theāḥju’s death, the next senior member assumed the role, and the mask was ceremonially transferred to his home. Because this system of private guardianship became increasingly complex and impractical, the presentdyaḥcheṃwas constructed through collective community effort. Over time, additional buildings were added, and the site has evolved into a large compound now used for weddings and other social or ritual gatherings.According to long-established custom, the residents of Patan must worship this Gaṇeśa after any auspicious communal meal (bhĩ bhway). The obligation applies after ritual feasts following life-cycle ceremonies, annualguthifeasts, musical processions, or any form of celebratory gathering. Similarly, after completing musical (bājā) or devotional-song (bhajan) training, students must perform music or sing before this Gaṇeśa to mark the successful conclusion of their instruction. In recent years, it has also become customary for couples to perform their wedding rituals seated before the image of Gaṇeśa.The smaller mask (LAL2970-002) has a special ritual function associated with theBuṅgadyahfestival. After the conclusion of theBuṅgadyah Jātrā, theguthiyārmembers of the festival procession carry the mask to Tamkhaḥ Dyaḥ (LAL0600) for ceremonial worship and later return it to its place in this shrine. Thepīṭha(CHO0100) of this Gaṇeśa is located across the Bagmatī River at Galchī in Cobhāra. Each year in the month of Kārttika, aKwayna Gaṇeśa khaṭ jātrā(procession of the deity’s palanquin) is held, during which the mask is carried to the Chobharpīṭhaand ceremonially brought back.
description_ne: ज्यापु समुदायका सात सदस्यीय गुठीमा जेष्ठ सदस्य आःजु हुने व्यवस्था छ जो यस द्यःछेँभित्र मरनोप्रान्त बस्नुपर्ने थिति चल्दै आएको छ ।पाटनको प्राचीन वस्तीभित्र पृथक पहिचान बोकेका तीन गणेश छन् । तीनमध्ये वस्तीको पूर्वमा स्थापित गणेशलाई थैना गणेश, पश्चिमकोलाई क्वय्‌ना गणेश र मध्य भागमा स्थापित गणेशलाई बुइना गणेश भनिन्छ । यी तीनै गणेशका नाम तिनको अवस्थितिका आधारमा गरिएको छ । 'थँ' को अर्थ नेवारीमा ‘माथि’ भन्ने हुन्छ । भैरवको कुममाथि चढेका गणेश भएकाले पाटनको पूर्वमा रहेका गणेशलाई थैना गणेश भनिएको हो । त्यसैगरी पाटनको पश्चिम भागमा रहेका क्वय्‌ना गणेश भैरवको मुनि बसेको प्रतिमामा देखाइन्छ । तल वा मुन्तिर जनाउन नेवारीमा 'क्वय्' शब्द प्रयोग हुन्छ । पाटनको मध्य भागमा स्थापित गणेश बुइना गणेशका नामले प्रसिद्ध छन् । 'बुइना'को अर्थ काखी च्यापिएका भन्ने हुन्छ । भैरवद्वारा काखी च्यापिएका गणेश (मध्य तहमा बसेका) भएबाट यिनलाई बुइना गणेश भनिएको हो । यसरी उत्तरमध्यकालमा पाटनभित्र पृथक प्रतिमालक्षणमा गणेश र भैरवका प्रतिमा व्युत्पादन हुन गयो (M. Ācārya VS 2079, p. 100-108) । यी तीनमध्ये यो क्वय्‌ना गणेशको द्यःछेँ हो । भैरवको मुनि बस्दै गरेको क्वय्‌ना गणेश मूर्ति पाटनमा अन्त पाइए तापनि यस द्यःछेँमा भने पित्तलको मुखाकृतिमात्र स्थापित छ । यस मुखाकृति नजिकै आकारमा सानो अर्को मुकाकृति छ जसलाई पनि क्वय्‌ना गणेश नै मानिन्छ । पित्तलको मुख्य मुखाकृतिलाई पित्तलकै सिंहासनभित्र राखिएको छ जुन विसं १९१८ (सन् १८६१) सालमा पाटनका एक अमात्यले चढाएका थिए । सिंहासन राखिएको कोठामा धातुका सिंह, ध्वजा एवं तोरण राखी सजाइएको छ । कंक्रिडको भवनमाथि फूचा (पुर) उठाई यस द्यःछेँ विसं २०३८ (सन् १९८१-८२) सालमा मात्र खडा भएको हो । यसपूर्व द्यःछेँ अवस्थित यस स्थान ऐतिहासिक पलेस्वांपुखू (कमलपोखरी) हुने गर्दथ्यो । पोखरीमाथि स्थानीयको वृहत श्रमदान पश्चात् यस द्यःछेँको निर्माणकार्य सम्भव भएको थियो (current āju, Maharjana, male, age 85) । क्वय्‌ना गणेश सम्बन्धी नःटोलमा एक पृथक चलन थियो । नःटोल, छाःबाहाः र चोभारका गरी कुल सातजना जेष्ठ ज्यापु सदस्य वरियता क्रमअनुसार क्वय्‌ना गणेशको गुठीमा रहन्छन् । तीमध्ये सबैभन्दा जेठा आःजु कहलाउँछ । विसं २०४० (सन् १९८३) सालमा यो द्यःछेँ बन्नु पूर्व क्वय्‌ना गणेशको मुखाकृति (LAL2970-001) आःजुको निजी आवासमा राख्ने थिति थियो । पाटनवासी आःजुकै आवासमा गई पूजा सम्पन्न गरी निजी घरमै भोज आयोजन गर्ने गर्दथे । आःजुको देहावसानपछि अर्का जेष्ठ आःजु हुन्थे र मुखाकृति नयाँ आजुको घरमा सारिन्थ्यो । यसरी आफ्नै निवासमा राख्ने थिति जटिल र अव्यवहारिक ठान्दै जनसहभागिताबाट यो द्यःछेँ निर्माण गरिएको थियो । क्रमश यहाँ अन्य भवन थपिँदै हाल ठुलो परिसरको रूप लिएको छ जहाँ विवाह लगायत अन्य संस्कार एवं भोज आयोजना हुन थालेको छ ।पाटनवासीले कुनैपनि शुभभोज (भिंभ्वय्) सम्पन्न पश्चात् यस गणेशलाई अनिवार्य पुज्नुपर्ने थिति छ । संस्कार पछिको भोज, गुथिको वार्षिक भोज, बाजा निकालिँदाको उत्सव भोज एवं कुनै पनि प्रकृतिको शुभकार्य पश्चात् भोज आयोजन भएमा त्यसको भोलिपल्ट अनिवार्य यहाँ पूज्न आउनुपर्ने थिति छ । बाजागाजा एवं भजन प्रशिक्षणको समाप्तिपछि पनि यहाँ बाजा बजाई वा भजन गाए पश्चात् मात्र प्रशिक्षण पूर्ण हुने मान्यत रही आएको छ । आजभोलि गणेशको मुखाकृतिको अग्र भागमा बसी विवाह गर्न आउनेको थिति पनि चलेको छ । यहाँ भएको सानो मुखाकृति (LAL2970-002) भने बुङ्गद्यः जात्रा समापन पश्चात् तम्कःद्य (LAL0600) मा हुने पूजाका खातिर उक्त मन्दिरमा लान बुङ्गद्यःका गुठीयारले लिन आउने र फर्काउने थिति छ । यस गणेशको पीठ (CHO0100) भने बागमती नदी पारी चोभारस्थित गल्छीमा छ । पीठसम्म मुखाकृति लग्ने र फर्काउने गरी कार्तिक महिनामा क्वय्‌ना गणेशको खटजात्रा हुने गर्दछ ।

historical_events.event_description: The family of Jita Govinda Amātya from Daubāhāḥ Ṭol offered a brass throne (siṃhāsana) to Kwayna Gaṇeśa, inviting the deity’s presence into their neighborhood through the consecration of the mask (mukhākṛti).

The construction of the presentdyaḥcheṃwas completed with financial support from Prince Dhirendra Śāha, on the occasion of King Virendra’s 39th birthday. The project was carried out under the supervision of the then Minister Jogmeyara Śreṣṭha, with additional material and financial contributions from the local community. A detailed record documenting the nature and extent of local donations was inscribed and preserved at the site.
The concrete roof (ḍhalān) of the second floor of the adjoiningsattalawas laid with the collective physical, financial, and voluntary labor (śramadāna) of the local residents.
Within thedyaḥcheṃcomplex, a new toilet facility was constructed, and the interior and exterior walls of the compound were plastered through local community support.

As the oldkhaṭa(palanquin) used in the annual procession of Kwayna Gaṇeśa had become dilapidated, a new one was built through community contributions, and the festival was celebrated with the participation of various musical ensembles (bājā).
The smaller mask of Gaṇeśa (LAL2970-002), which had deteriorated over time, was replicated and restored by the family of Hari Maharjana, preserving the original design.
In memory of Nhucchelāla Maharjana, his sons Surya and Devendra Maharjana decorated the roof above the main entrance of thedyaḥcheṃcomplex with brass plating.
The descendants of the lateāḥjuBulāla Maharjana offered anāgaornament made of 98.84tolaof silver to adorn the image of Gaṇeśa.
Omlāla Śreṣṭha and his family members collectively dedicated a silverkikipā(forehead ornament) to embellish the mask of Kavyna Gaṇeśa.
